newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco mayor to push $100 mln stadium bond.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco mayor to push $100 mln stadium bond.

text.p: San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown and the 49ers football team will propose a plan Monday to place a $100 million bond measure on the June ballot to help pay for a new stadium, the mayor's spokeswoman said.
The bond plan will be presented Monday to San Francisco Board of Supervisors, Brown spokeswoman Kandace Bender said. She said the details of the plan will be unveiled then.

Under the mayor's plan, finalized this week, $100 million of lease-revenue bonds would be issued to help pay for the National League Football team's proposed $300-million-plus stadium and retail complex, Bender said.
The bonds would be backed by revenues from a shopping mall the team intends to build as part of the sports complex.
The 49ers would cover the remaining stadium costs with revenues generated by the project, including the sale of luxury boxes, tickets and advertising, Bender said.
If placed on the ballot, the lease-revenue bonds would only require a simple majority to pass.
